One of the oldest Hindu temples in Sikkim, in the heart of Gangtok on MG Marg. Built in 1935 on land donated by the erstwhile Chogyal of Sikkim, it is the point of convergence for Gangtok's Hindu community, housing almost all major deities. Upgraded to a major temple complex in 1945-47; further works (multipurpose hall and library) began in 2011. A four-day Chhath Puja (Surya worship) is organised here annually, and light-and-sound shows run in the evenings in season. town_description: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, set in the Kangchenjunga hills at about 5,400 ft. The MG Marg pedestrian mall forms the heart of the town, and Gangtok blends Buddhist monasteries with Hindu temples such as Thakurbari, Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok.
